title: Obtain the decisive Russian document set
goal: Establish the reserve’s last separately identifiable custody and the first documented disposal.
basis: Schipor’s 1919/1921 comparison and document 121 are central; the full book and original archive annexes were not obtained.
request: Please identify and provide research copies, including annexes and adjacent folios, for the gold inventory dated 14 August 1919, the RGAE report of 23 May 1921, and the report of 13 December 1924 reproduced as document 121, pp. 339–340, in Ilie Schipor, Destinul Tezaurului României (2021). Please include complete archive shelfmarks and any outgoing-voucher references.
success: Authentic facsimiles with complete identifiers; a reproducible denomination/weight comparison; named recipients or voucher numbers.
stop: A summary repeating the author’s conclusion without tables or original references does not complete this lead.
access: Publisher/library access first; then holding archives. No purchase or request was made.

title: Audit GARF’s 1924 “depersonalized” entry
goal: Determine what обезличено meant in this specific account.
basis: Pokivaylova p. 132 cites GARF f. 374, op. 28, d. 861, l. 91.
request: Прошу уточнить возможность получения исследовательской копии: ГА РФ, ф. 374, оп. 28, д. 861, л. 91, включая оборот и соседние листы, относящиеся к румынскому золоту. Просьба сообщить заголовок дела, дату документа, автора и наличие приложений о движении золота.
success: A complete entry that distinguishes accounting consolidation, physical remelting and actual transfers; references to follow-on documents.
stop: Do not infer a melting date from the isolated word. Check that the cited folio actually supports the claim and whether its citation has shifted.
access: Shelfmark is as cited in a published book; catalogue and current access status not independently confirmed. Russian request is a working draft.

title: Recover the intelligence behind the US memorandum
goal: Turn an authentic Romanian allegation into a testable shipment claim.
basis: FRUS 1921 II, doc. 733, file 871.51/251, dated 15 August 1921.
request: Please identify the complete file and associated enclosures behind the Romanian Legation memorandum of 15 August 1921, State Department decimal file 871.51/251, published as FRUS 1921, volume II, document 733. We seek the source of the allegation, follow-up correspondence and any named ships, banks, customs entries or assay lots. Please confirm the modern series and box reference.
success: An enclosure or reply naming a lot, bank, ship or informant, which can be independently checked.
stop: If the file only repeats rumor and contains no identifiers, retain it as a contemporary allegation and reduce its priority.
access: US National Archives / Office of the Historian discovery route. A modern box number has not been established; the decimal file is real.

title: Match Soviet exports to Swedish mint and Western receipts
priority: A · Conditional on a shipment identifier
goal: Test a physical gold route across three independent institutions.
basis: US Treasury documents explain Swedish mint-stamp treatment; the 1924 translated report says coins went abroad.
request: For a matched 1921–1924 date and lot, seek Narkomfin dispatch and insurance vouchers, Swedish mint receiving and melt books, export records, and the destination bank or assay-office receipt. Record date, gross/fine mass, denomination, sender, recipient, batch number and account. Do not start by assuming every Soviet lot was Romanian.
success: A three-way match with a Romanian origin identifier before remelting, and a continuous financial or physical chain afterward.
stop: No Romanian link means a generic Soviet-gold route, not a discovery. Stop attributing once continuity is lost; describe that loss explicitly.
access: Exact Swedish repository series not yet established. Use official mint/Riksbank/archive catalogues; no bank was contacted.

title: Follow the Austrian crowns into the Issue Section
goal: Avoid assuming every coin went overseas.
basis: The 1924 report separately says Austrian crowns went to the State Bank’s Issue Section; the first-shipment table attributes about 29.31% of BNR value to Austrian crowns.
request: Request the State Bank Issue Section receiving ledgers and Narkomfin transfer orders for Austrian gold crowns from Romanian deposits, 1921–1925. Seek original treasury/case references, denomination totals, valuation basis and any subsequent reclassification or minting instructions.
success: A receiving entry matched to the Romanian-origin outgoing record and a subsequent disposition.
stop: A generic Austrian-crown balance is insufficient: this currency circulated widely.
access: Repository and series must be established from the original 1924 report’s references.

title: Reconcile cultural objects one by one
priority: A · Best prospect for identifiable surviving objects
goal: Produce a defensible missing-object register, distinct from monetary gold.
basis: MNIR’s 2016 announcement identifies National Art Museum return-inventory registers exhibited from the 1956 restitution. Lapedatu documents specific cultural shipments.
request: Vă rog să indicați inventarele de expediție din 1917 și registrele de primire din 1935 și 1956 pentru bunurile evacuate la Moscova. Pentru fiecare obiect neidentificat, căutăm numărul de inventar vechi și nou, descrierea, fotografia, dimensiunile, materialul, instituția deținătoare și eventualele procese-verbale de transfer. Solicitarea este pentru cercetare documentară, nu pentru inițierea unei revendicări.
success: An object-level difference list with images and stable identifiers; subsequent museum or sale records that can be checked.
stop: A difference in crate counts is not a missing-object list. Exclude documented returns and items never shipped.
access: MNIR, National Art Museum, Academy and depositing institutions. Registers located by description; underlying pages not yet obtained. Romanian text is a working draft.

title: Test the twelve-coin donation at MNIR
goal: Determine whether any small physical sample has documentary Moscow provenance.
basis: Reporting describes 12 French/Belgian coins, 77.09 g, donated on 6 March 2008; reported references 867 and 1272 require confirmation.
request: Vă rog să confirmați existența și cotele dosarului donației din 6 martie 2008 privind 12 monede de aur franceze și belgiene, cu masa totală relatată de 77,09 g. În presă apar numerele 867 și 1272, neconfirmate de noi. Căutăm fișele de inventar, declarația de proveniență, expertiza, fotografiile și orice document care leagă monedele de depozitul românesc din Moscova din 1916–1917.
success: A museum-confirmed accession plus documents bridging Russia and the donor; separate expert findings on coin authenticity and provenance.
stop: If only the donor’s assertion links them to Moscow, label provenance unproven. Do not extrapolate 12 coins to the full reserve.
access: No museum file inspected or request sent.

title: Identify the Danish newspaper behind the July 1920 claim
goal: Move one step closer to the earliest alleged Western disposal.
basis: Glasul Bucovinei no. 465, 10 July 1920, as quoted by Oprea; digitized collection located.
request: Obtain the complete issue, including neighboring columns, corrections and following issues. Transcribe the Copenhagen attribution exactly. Search Danish papers in the preceding weeks for rumænsk guld, rumænske guldmønter, 20 lei, russisk guld and Romanian/Roumanian variants; only then identify banks and their records.
success: Original report with named source and, ideally, bank or shipment identifiers; a correction or retraction is equally valuable.
stop: An unsourced chain of repeated press stories remains one allegation, however many newspapers printed it.
access: LIBRARIA / Arcanum collection located; exact issue not inspected, account access may be needed.

title: Separate Boyle’s cargo from his legend
goal: Establish exactly which records, banknotes and jewels were recovered in 1917.
basis: Rodney rejects bullion/jewels; Swain retells a Hill-derived jewels account; the 1924 report mentions royal brilliants in 1919.
request: Request the relevant December 1917 mission and cargo records in the Boyle papers cited as PRONI D1943/1–3, particularly receiving lists and Romanian acknowledgements. Compare with Hill’s Go Spy the Land (1932), chapters 15–20, the two royal cases in 1916, and any 1919 removal inventory. Confirm catalogue references before ordering.
success: A cargo list and signed receiving record, cross-matched to identifiable royal objects or to paper-only cargo.
stop: A memoir anecdote or later congratulatory letter cannot independently identify the contents of a sealed royal case.
access: PRONI reference is from Swain; original file catalogue not independently checked. Kent’s finding aid locates later correspondence, not proof of a rescue.

title: Trace French protective custody and keys
goal: Clarify who could access the deposits after diplomatic rupture.
basis: French diplomatic finding aid identifies relevant correspondence and military-mission series.
request: Je recherche les pièces relatives à la garde des dépôts roumains à Moscou en 1917–1918, notamment la remise des clefs, les scellés, les inventaires et les protestations diplomatiques. L’instrument de recherche 124PO/1 mentionne les articles 63–64 et 66–67. Pourriez-vous confirmer les dossiers pertinents et leurs conditions de consultation, sans présumer que ces articles contiennent les pièces recherchées ?
success: A dated handover or access record naming the deposit and responsible persons; independent comparison with Romanian and Russian copies.
stop: Holding keys is not the same as physical control if guards or authorities changed. Do not infer continuous secure custody from a diplomatic title.
access: French finding aid inspected; underlying files not read. Draft not sent.

title: Check the 1922 balance discrepancy
goal: Determine whether apparently conflicting figures use different dates or asset boundaries.
basis: Pokivaylova p. 132 quotes 105,102,337.88 gold roubles from Osokina and 87,074,501.05 from Sirotkin; p. 131 cites February reports.
request: Obtain Osokina, Zoloto dlia industrializatsii, p. 364; Sirotkin, Zarubezhnoe zoloto Rossii, p. 305; and the Sokolnikov reports cited as RGASPI f. 5, op. 1, d. 1372, ll. 3–8. Transcribe dates, headings, unit definitions and whether values are physical stock, book balances or net available funds.
success: A explained difference grounded in complete documents, or a documented error in one secondary account.
stop: Do not average the balances, convert them into an exact tonnage without basis, or select the figure that best supports a favored theory.
access: Books and original folios not obtained in this session. Shelfmarks are published citations, not confirmed current retrieval entries.

title: Require a Romanian identifier before chasing eastern hoards
priority: C · Only after stronger records justify it
goal: Keep the Kolchak/Czech/Japan trail falsifiable and bounded.
basis: General Russian gold traveled east; a Romanian component is speculative in the inspected literature.
request: First obtain an outgoing Romanian-deposit record naming Kazan, a captured train, Czech custody or an eastern bank, or find a receiving record with matching case identifiers. Only then expand to Czech military finance, Vladivostok shipping, Japanese or Chinese bank archives.
success: A specific bridge from this deposit into that custody chain.
stop: Without the bridge, do not commission a field search, assume a lake/train story is relevant, or describe general Imperial gold as Romanian property.
access: No physical search target or verified present holding has been identified.
